findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category (or uncategorized_category_id) has no row
findings.body:
The migration runs `execute(...)[0]['id']` on the join of `categories` and `site_settings` where `name = 'embed_category'`. `site_settings` only stores non-default values, and `embed_category` defaults to `''`, so on most installs the query returns zero rows. `PG::Result#[0]` on an empty result raises an IndexError ("Index 0 is out of range").

The fallback lookup of `uncategorized_category_id` on line 15 has the same problem on a fresh database, where no site_settings rows exist yet.

Result: `rake db:migrate` aborts on fresh installs and on any existing site that never set `embed_category`, which blocks the upgrade. Check `ntuples`/`cmd_tuples` before indexing, or use `.first` with nil handling.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are not normalized, so existing scheme-prefixed hosts silently stop matching
findings.body:
The old `allows_embeddable_host?` accepted entries like `http://eviltrout.com` or `https://eviltrout.com`; it parsed them with `URI(h).host`, and the removed specs covered exactly this. The migration inserts each raw line verbatim with no scheme or path stripping and no trimming of whitespace or `\r` (it only splits on "\n"). It also bypasses the model's `before_validation` normalization.

`EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` then compares `lower(host)` against the bare `uri.host` (e.g. `eviltrout.com`). Any migrated entry that has a scheme, path, surrounding whitespace or a CRLF line ending never matches. Those sites lose embedding with no error after upgrading.

Strip `^https?://`, any path, and whitespace from each record before inserting it.

findings.title: Host values are string-interpolated into raw SQL
findings.body: `execute "INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` puts the site setting value directly into SQL without quoting. Any host string containing a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters) breaks the migration or injects arbitrary SQL. The value comes from admin input, but a migration should not trust stored data this way. Use `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)` or a parameterized insert.

findings.title: Host validation rejects many legitimate hosts
before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: `self.host.sub!(...)` is called unconditionally. If `host` is nil — for example `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?`, or a create/update request without `embeddable_host[host]` — this raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `if host.present?` or use `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...)`.

findings.title: Hosts saved with a port can never match
findings.body:
The validation regex explicitly allows a `:port` suffix, and `before_validation` strips only the scheme and path, so `example.com:8080` is stored as-is. `record_for_host` compares the stored value with `uri.host`, which never includes the port. Such entries are accepted by the UI but never allow embedding.

Relatedly, the stored value is lowercased in SQL but the argument is not. Ruby's `URI#host` preserves case, so a mixed-case referer host will not match. Either strip/compare ports consistently or reject ports, and downcase the argument.

findings.title: update/destroy raise 500 when the record is missing
findings.body: Both `update` and `destroy` use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then call methods on the result. When the id does not exist (for example, deleted in another tab), `save_host(nil)` or `nil.destroy` raises NoMethodError and the client gets a 500. Use `find` or `find_by!`, or raise `Discourse::NotFound`.

findings.title: category_id is not validated to exist
findings.body: Any `category_id` sent by the client is stored without checking that the category exists, and the model has no validation on the association. A bogus or later-deleted category id leaves a dangling reference. The admin list then shows an empty category badge, and imported topics silently fall back to uncategorized because TopicCreator cannot find the category.

findings.title: Plural `_ids` hydration always deletes the ids and can crash on null
findings.body:
For singular `_id` keys, the original id is kept unless a hydrated object is found. The new plural branch behaves differently:
- It unconditionally `delete obj[k]` and replaces it with `obj[pluralize(subType)]`, an array of `_lookupSubType` results.
- When the payload has no side-loaded collection for that subtype, the array is full of `undefined` and the original ids are lost. This affects any existing `__rest_serializer` payload with an `*_ids` field such as `user_ids` or `group_ids`.
- If the value is `null`, `obj[k].map` throws a TypeError.
- The `hydrated || []` fallback is dead code, because `map` always returns an array.

Only replace the field when the lookups succeed, and guard against non-array values.

findings.title: Feed-imported topics lose their category when the article host is not registered
findings.body: Previously every imported topic went to `SiteSetting.embed_category`. Now the category comes from the `EmbeddableHost` matching the article URL's host. Feed-polled articles whose links point to a host not in the table (e.g. feed on `feeds.example.com`, articles on `blog.example.com`) get `category: nil` and land in uncategorized. Existing feed setups can silently change behaviour after upgrade.

findings.title: Client shows no category after saving without choosing one
findings.body: If the admin saves without picking a category, `categoryId` is null. The server substitutes `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`, but the client sets `host.category` to `Discourse.Category.findById(null)`, which is undefined. It ignores the `category_id` returned in the response. The row shows no category badge until the page is reloaded.

findings.title: Delete failures are silently swallowed
findings.body: `destroyRecord().then(...)` has no `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, unlike `save`. If the DELETE request fails (403, 500, network error), the admin gets no feedback and the row stays with no indication of what happened.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents are swapped
findings.body: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator. The new `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`). It works only because all fabricators are loaded globally, but anyone looking for the category fabricators will find them in the wrong file. Swap the contents back.

findings.title: Test name no longer matches what it tests
findings.body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer looks at embeddable hosts. The test "is false if embeddable_host is blank" passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and there is no TopicEmbed. Likewise, `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` in the nested context has no effect on the result. The spec suggests behaviour the code no longer has. It also hides the behaviour change: topics are now expandable even when no hosts are configured.

findings.title: 'find embedded' test requests fruit 2 but asserts fruit 1's data
findings.body: The test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` (banana, `color_ids: [3]`) and asserts two colors with ids 1 and 2, which are apple's colors. It passes only because the pretender `/fruits/:id` handler always returns `fruits[0]`. If the stub ever honours the id, the test breaks, and as written it does not check that the requested record is the one hydrated.
